# Read before quoting any figure

*Independent research compiled from public records for informational purposes only. Not legal, medical, or investment advice. Evidence tiers: **A** documented, **B** corroborated, **C** claimed — B and C may not be quoted as established fact. Causes are reported as attributed, never asserted. This dataset does not corroborate, and is not corroborated by, any other dataset in this corpus. See `meta/IS_META_terms.md`.*

Constraints that apply to everything in this folder.

**50 entries.**

- [—] US series age-adjusted to 2000 US standard population; annual 2001-2021 from NCHS db464 tables, 2022-2024 from db509/541/548, 1999 from db362. No US 2025 figure yet — provisional 2025 counts expected via CDC WONDER/NVSS later in 2026.

- [—] CDC Vital Signs June 2018 analyzed persons aged >=10; its rates not directly comparable to all-ages age-adjusted NCHS rates; its '~30% since 1999' is the origin of the claim under review.

- [—] Cross-country 'WHO' rows are WHO Global Health Estimates (age-standardized to WHO world standard population) via World Bank API mirror (SH.STA.SUIC.P5); modeled estimates differ in level from national vital registration (e.g., WHO Canada 2021 = 9.4 vs PHAC 11.8). Use WHO rows for trend comparison, national rows for latest levels.

- [—] UK: ONS figures are England & Wales registrations, not UK-wide occurrences; only 38.7% of 2024 registrations occurred in 2024 (coroner delays) — occurrence-based rates broadly stable since 2018. UK definition includes deaths of undetermined intent (15+), inflating rates relative to some countries.

- [—] Japan: NPA/MHLW suicide statistics (2025: 19,097; rate 15.4) compiled differently from vital-statistics causes of death; crude rates.

- [—] Australia 2024 (11.9), Canada 2024 count (4,394), South Korea 2024 (28.3; 14,439) are preliminary/subject to revision.

- [—] Germany 12.2 (2023) is a crude resident rate; EU-standardized German rate 10.3 in 2021 vs EU average 10.2 (Destatis).

- [—] Divergence answer: yes — the US long-run rise (~+30-35% since 1999/2002) diverges from peers. Japan, Germany, France declined substantially since 2000; Canada flat-to-declining; UK and Australia roughly flat with modest recent upticks; South Korea rose steeply to ~2010-2011, declined, remains OECD's highest, ticked up in 2024.

- [—] Per safe-reporting standards, method-specific figures intentionally excluded; only aggregate rates and counts reported.

- [—] WHO GHE values fetched via World Bank API mirror; WHO IRIS PDF returned 403 — headline findings verified from WHO's news release and fact sheet.

- [—] Small discrepancies between the 2019 report's global rate (9.0) and GHE-2021-revision value for 2019 (9.42); series internally consistent within one source, not mixable across sources.

- [—] WHO GHE figures for China, Russia, India are modeled estimates, not counted deaths; countries included by design — the data-quality problem is reported as a finding, not a reason for exclusion.

- [—] NCRB ADSI 2022 PDF robots-blocked; count tier B via CMHLP; rate and 2017-2022 trend tier A via peer-reviewed analysis.

- [—] Million Death Study absolute count not verifiable from a fetchable page; represented by the peer-reviewed rate comparison (22 vs ~11.4).

- [—] Rosstat not fetched directly; Rosstat-based figures via peer-reviewed EJPH analysis (conference-supplement abstract) and 2024 Population and Economics article.

- [—] Frontiers 2025 corrected global total (>1M/yr) is a peer-reviewed MODELED estimate; present as such.

- [—] Safe-reporting: rates and counts only; method details deliberately not extracted.

- [—] WHO fact sheet 727,000 / 73% LMIC = 2021 (GHE 2021); 700,000+/36% decline = 2019 (GHE 2019). Label years explicitly in visualizations.

- [—] Provisional vs final overdose counts differ: May 2026 release compares provisional 2025 (69,973) vs provisional 2024 (81,313); final 2024 is 79,384. Do not mix provisional and final in one series.

- [—] Gallup depression = self-reported lifetime/current diagnosis, not clinically assessed prevalence; rising diagnosis can reflect help-seeking, screening, reduced stigma as well as true incidence — different construct from NSDUH MDE or PHQ-8.

- [—] NSDUH 2021+ uses redesigned multimode methodology, not directly comparable with pre-2020 NSDUH; do not splice.

- [—] WHO 25% pandemic increase is a modeled first-pandemic-year estimate, not diagnoses; WHO baselines since revised (depression 5.7% adults / ~332M; anxiety 359M in 2021).

- [—] Cancer incidence trends can be inflated/masked by screening and diagnostic change; BMJ Oncology global counts (+79%) are raw counts affected by population growth, not age-standardized rates; 2020 incidence depressed by pandemic diagnosis disruptions.

- [—] SEER 'stable' all-sites incidence coexists with rising site- and demographic-specific trends.

- [—] US-vs-peer life expectancy gap depends on comparator set (Peterson-KFF: 3.7 yrs in 2024). OECD Health at a Glance 2025 US note not directly fetchable (robots/403) — cited only via Peterson-KFF.

- [—] ACS 2026 projections are model-based estimates, not registrations; actual incidence data through 2022, mortality through 2023.

- [—] Diagnoses vs prescriptions must not be blurred: every Tier A epidemiology source shows stable-to-declining age-standardised schizophrenia prevalence/incidence, while every Tier A prescribing dataset shows rising volumes — cited authors attribute the gap to off-label use, expanded indications, demographics, access; not rising disease.

- [—] England 'items' count dispensing events, not people or doses; items, fills, DDDs, and %-of-population are different measures, not directly comparable.

- [—] Hong Kong study (PMID 39961232) cited by identity only — retrieve exact figures before publishing numbers from it.

- [—] England 2024/25 class-level antipsychotic (13.9m) and hypnotic/anxiolytic (13.4m) items corroborated via The Pharmacist (tier B); canonical values in NHSBSA Excel tables. NHSBSA issued a Jan 2026 correction for patient double-counting in some calendar-year tables — re-check patient counts.

- [—] ASPE = IQVIA Total Patient Tracker projections (SSRIs only for antidepressants — understates total); CDC MMWR = commercially insured only; DEA/IQVIA LRx ~94% of retail — none is a full census.

- [—] GBD 'stable prevalence' is modeled with wide uncertainty in low-data regions; registry incidence measures treated/diagnosed cases, sensitive to service coverage and coding.

- [—] Market-size figures (tier C) are proprietary forecasts, not measured data.

- [—] OECD DDD figures corroborated via Euronews (tier B); primary reference: https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/health-at-a-glance-2023_7a7afb35-en/full-report/pharmaceutical-consumption_4b6cb013.html

- [—] All rows are attributions as stated by the cited source, not asserted causes; several sources themselves flag correlational evidence.

- [—] CDC Vital Signs 2018: suicide rarely caused by a single factor; 54% = no *known* mental health condition — undiagnosed conditions cannot be ruled out.

- [—] Case & Deaton supporting line quoted from Brookings' official publication page summary; deaths-of-despair framing scholarly contested (Ruhm c07; other critiques exist, not fetched).

- [—] HRSA figures are 2038 projections based on current utilization, explicitly excluding unmet need; page updated Dec 2025.

- [—] WHO suicide fact sheet and CDC opioid epidemic page are living documents; dates are last-updated as displayed 2026-08-19.

- [—] Surgeon General doc_dates at month precision where fetched PDF displayed only year.

- [—] Per safe-reporting standards, no suicide method details; firearm access named only as access-level risk factor.

- [—] Twenge et al. (c10) remains contested; both attribution and principal critique (c14) included so the register carries the dispute, not a resolution.

- [—] All tier-A documents fetched and confirmed to contain quoted/near-verbatim lines on 2026-08-19.

- [—] Health is NOT the most-deployed domain: public-admin 151, defence-intel 33, health 32, law-enforcement 31. Phrase health as the largest citizen-facing service domain / third overall.

- [—] deployments.json contains no date fields; all temporal claims about deployments come from milestones.json (occurred_on) or year mentions in workload strings.

- [—] 'Live' = status=production. Pandemic-response has 1 accredited row counted as neither live nor decommissioned.

- [—] geographies.json: 35 rows, 32 country-level (EU, INTL supranational; US-CO sub-national).

- [—] regulations.json: exactly 99 rows, 8 neural_data=true (one proposed); '0 of 99 record recourse' structurally confirmed — no recourse/redress/appeal field exists in the schema.

- [—] WebFetch truncates deployments.json (~148KB); counts were parsed from complete raw JSON, not summarized extractions.

- [—] Every row is structural or pattern only; no row asserts or implies causation; tier grades reflect strength of the documented overlap, never strength of any causal story.

# How much the numbers can be trusted

*Independent research compiled from public records for informational purposes only. Not legal, medical, or investment advice. Evidence tiers: **A** documented, **B** corroborated, **C** claimed — B and C may not be quoted as established fact. Causes are reported as attributed, never asserted. This dataset does not corroborate, and is not corroborated by, any other dataset in this corpus. See `meta/IS_META_terms.md`.*

Counting, coverage and definitional problems, each documented by a named body.

**15 entries.**

### Global — dq01
[A] documented by WHO — WHO · Suicide data <https://www.who.int/teams/mental-health-and-substance-use/data-research/suicide-data>

Most WHO Member States lack good-quality vital registration for suicide

*Quantification:* 86 of 183 Member States have good-quality vital registration (GHE 2021); the 37 LMICs with good registration account for only 16.3% of estimated LMIC suicides; 73% of global suicides occur in LMICs.

*Document:* WHO suicide data page + fact sheet

### Global — dq02
[A] documented by WHO — WHO · Suicide data <https://www.who.int/teams/mental-health-and-substance-use/data-research/suicide-data>

Systematic misclassification of suicides into other ICD categories

*Quantification:* Most commonly misclassified as deaths of undetermined intent (Y10-Y34), accidents (V01-X59), homicides (X85-Y09), unknown cause; 'under-reporting and misclassification are greater problems for suicide than for most other causes of death.'

*Document:* WHO suicide data page

### Russia — dq03
[A] documented by Semyonova, Sabgayda, Zubko & Gavrilov — European Journal of Public Health · Semyonova et al. — Russian suicide mortality: official and actual rates <https://academic.oup.com/eurpub/article/30/Supplement_5/ckaa166.1371/5915576>

Rising share of Russian deaths coded 'undetermined intent' masks suicides; official decline overstated

*Quantification:* Official suicide mortality fell 3.4x (M) / 2.9x (F) 2000-2018 but undetermined-intent deaths fell only 14.2% / 11.6%; true suicide mortality likely exceeds Rosstat by ~60% (M) and >2x (F); latent events >1/3 (M) and ~50% (F) of total by 2018.

*Document:* European Journal of Public Health 30(Suppl 5), 2020

### Russia — dq04
[A] documented by Semyonova, Zubko & Sabgayda — Population and Economics · Semyonova, Zubko & Sabgayda — Undercounting of Age-Specific Suicide Mortality <https://populationandeconomics.pensoft.net/article/107534/>

Age-specific quantification of latent suicides in Russian undetermined-intent coding

*Quantification:* Counting relevant undetermined-intent deaths as latent suicides increases male estimated losses from ~80% (15-24) declining to ~50% at older ages; female suicide mortality rate doubles at all ages above 15.

*Document:* Population and Economics (2024)

### China — dq05
[A] documented by BMC Public Health (2024) analysis of NHC death registration — BMC Public Health · Long-term changing patterns of suicide mortality in China 1987-2020 <https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-18743-z>

China's mortality registration historically covered ~10% of population, unrepresentative (eastern/central cities)

*Quantification:* 'Mortality data in the early years only covered approximately 10% of China's population'; stigma-driven underreporting 'may affect the authenticity of suicide data.'

*Document:* 'Long-term changing patterns of suicide mortality in China 1987-2020'

### China — dq06
[A] documented by Phillips, Li & Zhang — The Lancet · Phillips, Li & Zhang — Suicide rates in China, 1995-99 <https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(02)07954-0/abstract>

China's 1990s national figures required explicit adjustment for unreported deaths

*Quantification:* Adjusted official data to 23/100k and 287,000 deaths/yr; rural 3x urban, female 25% above male — patterns invisible in urban-weighted registration.

*Document:* The Lancet 359(9309), 2002

### India — dq07
[A] documented by RGI Million Death Study (Patel et al., Lancet 2012), via peer-reviewed review — Shanghai Archives of Psychiatry · Indian suicide data review (Million Death Study) <https://shanghaiarchivesofpsychiatry.org/en/2014.02.003.html>

India's official statistics are police-reported (NCRB/FIR); verbal autopsy finds ~2x the official rate

*Quantification:* Verbal-autopsy 2010 rate ages 15+: 22/100k vs NCRB ~11.4; rural verbal-autopsy rates 3-4x government-reported.

*Document:* Shanghai Archives of Psychiatry (2014)

### India — dq08
[B] documented by CMHLP (citing GBD) — CMHLP · Is India's suicide data accurate? NCRB vs GBD <https://cmhlp.org/blogs/data-is-the-new-oil-but-not-when-it-comes-to-suicides-in-india/>

GBD modeled estimates for India substantially exceed NCRB, with gendered undercount

*Quantification:* GBD 2016 75% above NCRB; 802,684 additional deaths 2005-2015; undercount ~27% male / ~50% female; poisoning deaths often recorded as accidental.

*Document:* CMHLP blog on India suicide data accuracy

### India — dq09
[B] documented by Parliament of India; CMHLP — Wikipedia · Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_Healthcare_Act,_2017>

Legal history suppressed Indian reporting: attempted suicide criminal (IPC 309) until Mental Healthcare Act 2017

*Quantification:* Passed 2017-04-07, in force 2018-05-29; families still withhold information; 'misconceptions about legal consequences persist.'

*Document:* Mental Healthcare Act 2017 (S.115)

### Global (≥24 countries) — dq10
[B] documented by United for Global Mental Health (corroborated by WHO) — United for Global Mental Health · Suicide Decriminalisation <https://unitedgmh.org/suicide-decriminalisation/>

Criminalization of suicide/attempts in ≥24 countries deters help-seeking and drives misclassification

*Quantification:* 'In at least 24 countries anyone who attempts suicide can be arrested, prosecuted, or punished'; WHO: illegality makes under-reporting and misclassification greater problems.

*Document:* 'Decriminalising Suicide: Saving Lives, Reducing Stigma' (2025 update)

### UK (England & Wales) — dq11
[A] documented by ONS — ONS · Change in the standard of proof used by coroners <https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/birthsdeathsandmarriages/deaths/articles/changeinthestandardofproofusedbycoronersandtheimpactonsuicidedeathregistrationsdatainenglandandwales/2020-12-08>

Definitional divergence: UK deliberately INCLUDES undetermined-intent deaths (Y10-Y34, 15+) in 'suicide' — official rates not like-for-like across countries

*Quantification:* Definition = X60-X84 (10+) plus Y10-Y34 (15+); from 2018-07-26 coroners' standard of proof lowered to 'balance of probabilities', after which intentional self-harm coding rose and undetermined intent fell.

*Document:* 'Change in the standard of proof used by coroners...' (ONS, 2020-12-08)

### Global — dq12
[A] documented by WHO — WHO · Global Health Estimates <https://www.who.int/data/global-health-estimates>

WHO headline numbers for most countries are modeled estimates (GHE), not counted deaths — incl. China, India, Russia

*Quantification:* Estimates produced from consolidated sources incl. GBD models where registration is missing; only 86/183 states have good registration.

*Document:* WHO Global Health Estimates page (GHE 2021)

### Global — dq13
[B] documented by Our World in Data — Our World in Data · How do global statistics on suicide differ between sources? <https://ourworldindata.org/how-do-global-statistics-on-suicide-differ-between-sources>

WHO and IHME/GBD produce materially different estimates for the same country-years (different models, undetermined-intent redistribution)

*Quantification:* WHO uses adjusted registration where coverage >=80%; IHME reclassifies some undetermined-intent deaths to suicide; India lacks usable WHO Mortality Database registration data.

*Document:* 'How do global statistics on suicide differ between sources?'

### Global; LMICs — dq14
[A] documented by Meda et al. (systematic review + meta-analysis) — Frontiers in Psychiatry · Meda et al. — How many people die by suicide each year? Not 727,000 <https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychiatry/articles/10.3389/fpsyt.2025.1609580/full>

Aggregate global underreporting: ~1 in 6 suicides missing worldwide; ~1 in 3 in large LMICs (India, China)

*Quantification:* Pooled global underreporting 17.9% (CI 10.9-28.1%); LMICs 'such as India and China' 34.9% (CI 20.3-53%); HICs 11.5% (CI 6.6-19.3%); corrected global total >1 million/yr.

*Document:* Frontiers in Psychiatry (2025)

### US — hq015
[A] documented by not stated — CDC/NCHS · U.S. Overdose Deaths Decrease for Third Consecutive Year in 2025 (provisional) <https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/pressroom/releases/20260513.html>

The 2025 figure is provisional and the 2024 figure on this chart is final. They are different vintages, and the choice of vintage changes the headline. CDC's May 2026 release reports a fall of almost 14% for 2025 by comparing it with a provisional 2024 estimate of 81,313. Measured against the final 2024 count of 79,384, the same provisional 2025 figure is a fall of about 11.9%. Provisional counts rise as late certificates are processed, so the 2025 number should be expected to revise upward.

*Quantification:* none given

*Document:*

# Dated milestones

*Independent research compiled from public records for informational purposes only. Not legal, medical, or investment advice. Evidence tiers: **A** documented, **B** corroborated, **C** claimed — B and C may not be quoted as established fact. Causes are reported as attributed, never asserted. This dataset does not corroborate, and is not corroborated by, any other dataset in this corpus. See `meta/IS_META_terms.md`.*

The health track of the site's master timeline. Co-occurrence with anything else on that timeline is not relation.

**30 entries.**

- **1999-01** [A] Overdose record begins: 16,849 deaths — The first year of the modern comparable series. Age-adjusted rate 6.1 per 100,000. Every later figure on this track is measured against this. — CDC/NCHS · Data tables for NCHS Data Brief 428: Drug Overdose Deaths in the United States, 1999-2020 <https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/databriefs/db428-tables.pdf>

- **2002-03-09** [A] Lancet publishes first adjusted national suicide rates for China (1995-99) — Phillips, Li & Zhang: 23/100k (~287,000 deaths/yr) after adjusting for unreported deaths; rural 3x urban; baseline for China's later decline to WHO-estimated 8.75 by 2019. — The Lancet · Phillips, Li & Zhang — Suicide rates in China, 1995-99 <https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(02)07954-0/abstract>

- **2006-01-01** [A] Russia implements 2006 alcohol control policy — Later attributed an immediate, permanent ~9% reduction in male suicide mortality (~4,000 male lives/yr) — part of Russia's decline from among the world's highest rates. — AJPH via PMC · Pridemore et al. — 2006 Russian Alcohol Policy and Male Suicide Mortality <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3828708/>

- **2010-01** [A] Second wave of opioid epidemic begins (heroin) — CDC dates the second wave to 2010. Overdose deaths that year: 38,329 — already more than double 1999, before fentanyl enters the record. — CDC · Understanding the Opioid Overdose Epidemic <https://www.cdc.gov/overdose-prevention/about/understanding-the-opioid-overdose-epidemic.html>

- **2013-01** [A] Third wave of opioid epidemic begins (illicit fentanyl) — CDC dates the third wave of opioid overdose deaths to 2013, driven by illicitly manufactured fentanyl (see W4 c09 source). — CDC · Understanding the Opioid Overdose Epidemic <https://www.cdc.gov/overdose-prevention/about/understanding-the-opioid-overdose-epidemic.html>

- **2016-01** [A] Synthetic-opioid acceleration: 63,632 deaths (+21.4%) — The steepest year of the fentanyl wave to that point, three years after it began. Age-adjusted rate 19.8 per 100,000, more than triple 1999. — CDC/NCHS · Data tables for NCHS Data Brief 428: Drug Overdose Deaths in the United States, 1999-2020 <https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/databriefs/db428-tables.pdf>

- **2017-04-07** [B] India passes Mental Healthcare Act 2017, decriminalizing attempted suicide — In force 2018-05-29; presumption of severe stress supersedes IPC 309 — directly relevant to India's police-report undercount. — Wikipedia · Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_Healthcare_Act,_2017>

- **2018-06-08** [A] CDC Vital Signs: suicide rates rising across the US — MMWR reports suicide rates rose ~30% since 1999, with significant increases in 44 states and >30% increases in 25 states (1999-2016). — CDC MMWR · Vital Signs: Trends in State Suicide Rates — United States, 1999-2016 (June 8, 2018) <https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/67/wr/mm6722a1.htm>

- **2018-07-26** [A] England & Wales lower coroners' standard of proof for suicide conclusions — Threshold moved to 'balance of probabilities'; intentional self-harm coding rose while undetermined intent fell — a natural experiment in how legal process shapes suicide statistics. — ONS · Change in the standard of proof used by coroners <https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/birthsdeathsandmarriages/deaths/articles/changeinthestandardofproofusedbycoronersandtheimpactonsuicidedeathregistrationsdatainenglandandwales/2020-12-08>

- **2020-01** [A] Largest single-year rise on record: 91,799 deaths (+30.0%) — The pandemic year. A rise of 21,169 deaths on 2019 — the largest one-year increase in the series, and the mirror of the 2024 decline. — CDC/NCHS · Data tables for NCHS Data Brief 428: Drug Overdose Deaths in the United States, 1999-2020 <https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/databriefs/db428-tables.pdf>

- **2021-06-17** [A] WHO releases 'Suicide worldwide in 2019: Global Health Estimates' — WHO reports >700,000 suicide deaths in 2019 (1 in 100 deaths), a 36% decline in the global age-standardized rate 2000-2019, declines in five regions, and a 17% rise in the Region of the Americas. — World Health Organization · One in 100 deaths is by suicide (launch of 'Suicide worldwide in 2019') <https://www.who.int/news/item/17-06-2021-one-in-100-deaths-is-by-suicide>

- **2021-12-07** [A] US Surgeon General advisory: Protecting Youth Mental Health — Rare public health advisory declaring a youth mental health crisis accelerated by the pandemic. — American Hospital Association · Surgeon general advisory targets youth mental health crisis (2021-12-07) <https://www.aha.org/news/headline/2021-12-07-surgeon-general-advisory-targets-youth-mental-health-crisis>

- **2022-01** [A] Overdose deaths peak: 107,941 — The maximum of the series and the point every subsequent decline is measured down from. Age-adjusted rate 32.6 per 100,000 — 6.4 times the 1999 count. — CDC/NCHS · NCHS Data Brief 522: Drug Overdose Deaths in the United States, 2003-2023 <https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db522.htm>

- **2022-03-02** [A] WHO: pandemic triggered 25% increase in global anxiety and depression — WHO scientific brief estimates global prevalence of anxiety and depression rose 25% in the first pandemic year. — WHO · COVID-19 pandemic triggers 25% increase in prevalence of anxiety and depression worldwide <https://www.who.int/news/item/02-03-2022-covid-19-pandemic-triggers-25-increase-in-prevalence-of-anxiety-and-depression-worldwide>

- **2022-07-16** [A] US launches 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline — The National Suicide Prevention Lifeline transitions to the three-digit 988 number for 24/7 crisis care nationwide. — US Federal Communications Commission · U.S. Transition to 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline Begins July 16 <https://www.fcc.gov/document/us-transition-988-suicide-crisis-lifeline-begins-july-16>

- **2022-10-12** [A] FDA announces nationwide Adderall shortage — Shortage of IR amphetamine mixed salts, citing Teva manufacturing delays and demand outstripping supply — start of multi-year ADHD-drug shortage. — FDA · FDA Announces Shortage of Adderall (2022-10-12) <https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/fda-announces-shortage-adderall>

- **2023-03-30** [A] CDC MMWR: stimulant prescription-fill trends — Fills rose 3.6% (2016) -> 4.1% (2021) of commercially insured, double-digit 2020-2021 jumps among adult women, linked to telehealth-era prescribing. — CDC MMWR · Danielson et al., Trends in Stimulant Prescription Fills 2016-2021 <https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/wr/mm7213a1.htm>

- **2023-09-05** [A] BMJ Oncology publishes global early-onset cancer study — GBD-based analysis: early-onset (under-50) cancer cases rose 79% worldwide 1990-2019, to 3.26 million. — BMJ Group (BMJ Oncology) · Global surge in cancers among the under 50s over past three decades <https://bmjgroup.com/global-surge-in-cancers-among-the-under-50s-over-past-three-decades/>

- **2024-02-26** [B] Pediatrics: youth antidepressant dispensing surged post-March 2020 — Dispensing to adolescents/young adults rose 63.5% faster after March 2020 than pre-pandemic trend (Chua et al.). — Pediatrics · Chua et al., Antidepressant Dispensing to US Adolescents and Young Adults: 2016-2022 (page 403 to proxy; verified via IHPI) <https://publications.aap.org/pediatrics/article/153/3/e2023064245/196655/Antidepressant-Dispensing-to-US-Adolescents-and>

- **2024-09** [A] NCHS confirms 2022 as record year for US suicide — NCHS Data Brief 509 reports 49,476 suicide deaths in 2022 and an age-adjusted rate of 14.2 — the highest since 1941 — up 30% from 2002. — CDC/NCHS · NCHS Data Brief 509: Suicide Mortality in the United States, 2002-2022 (Sept 2024) <https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db509.htm>

- **2024-09-26** [A] FDA approves Cobenfy (xanomeline + trospium) for schizophrenia — First antipsychotic targeting cholinergic rather than dopamine receptors — 'the first new approach to schizophrenia treatment in decades' (FDA). — FDA · FDA Approves Cobenfy (2024-09-26) <https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-drug-new-mechanism-action-treatment-schizophrenia>

- **2024-11-13** [A] DEA releases IQVIA report on US stimulant trends 2012-2023 — Prescriptions +60% (50.4m -> 80.8m); women overtook men for the first time in 2022-23. — IQVIA for DEA · Stimulant Prescription Trends in the United States, 2012-2023 <https://www.deadiversion.usdoj.gov/pubs/docs/IQVIA-Report-on-Stimulant-Trends-2024.pdf>

- **2025-02-25** [B] CDC announces ~24% decline in US overdose deaths — Provisional data (12 months ending Sept 2024): ~87,000 overdose deaths, ~27,000 fewer than prior year. — CDC · CDC Reports Nearly 24% Decline in U.S. Drug Overdose Deaths (2025-02-25, provisional) <https://www.cdc.gov/media/releases/2025/2025-cdc-reports-decline-in-us-drug-overdose-deaths.html>

- **2025-07-24** [A] NHSBSA publishes 2024/25 Medicines Used in Mental Health statistics — Record 92.6m antidepressant items; +24.3% one-year rise in adults prescribed ADHD medication; items and patients rose in 4 of 5 drug groups. — NHSBSA · Medicines Used in Mental Health – England – 2015/16 to 2024/25 <https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/statistical-collections/medicines-used-mental-health-england/medicines-used-mental-health-england-201516-202425>

- **2025-07-28** [A] SAMHSA releases 2024 NSDUH — Adolescent past-year MDE fell to 15.4% from 18.1% in 2023; adult any-mental-illness roughly stable at 23.4%. — SAMHSA · 2024 NSDUH Releases (2025-07-28) <https://www.samhsa.gov/data/data-we-collect/nsduh-national-survey-drug-use-and-health/national-releases/2024>

- **2025-09** [A] NCHS: 2023 US suicide rate essentially unchanged — NCHS Data Brief 541 reports 49,316 deaths and a rate of 14.1 in 2023 (-0.7% vs 2022, not statistically significant). — CDC/NCHS · NCHS Data Brief 541: Changes in Suicide Rates in the United States From 2022 to 2023 (Sept 2025) <https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db541.htm>

- **2026-01** [A] NCHS: US life expectancy hits 79.0; 2024 overdose deaths fell 26.2% — Data Brief 548: life expectancy +0.6 yr to 79.0, surpassing pre-pandemic. Data Brief 549: final 2024 overdose deaths 79,384. — CDC/NCHS · Mortality in the United States, 2024 (Data Brief 548, Jan 2026) <https://cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db548.htm>

- **2026-01-13** [A] ACS publishes Cancer Statistics 2026 — Projects 2,114,850 new US cases and 626,140 deaths in 2026; mortality down 34% since 1991; 5-year survival 70%. — American Cancer Society · Annual Cancer Statistics Report 2026 <https://pressroom.cancer.org/cancer-statistics-report-2026>

# Overlaps with the Government Cloud record

*Independent research compiled from public records for informational purposes only. Not legal, medical, or investment advice. Evidence tiers: **A** documented, **B** corroborated, **C** claimed — B and C may not be quoted as established fact. Causes are reported as attributed, never asserted. This dataset does not corroborate, and is not corroborated by, any other dataset in this corpus. See `meta/IS_META_terms.md`.*

Structural and pattern observations only. Two things occurring in the same period is a co-occurrence. Each entry carries its own note saying so, and neither dataset corroborates the other.

**12 entries.**

### US suicide rate rose ~30-35% 1999-2018 (CDC MMWR mm6722a1; NCHS db362); record 49,476 deaths 2022 (db509); overdose record 107,941 in 2022 (db549)
[A] both

**Gov Cloud fact:** deployments.json (399 rows, health=32, 29 production) records only id, geography, vendor, domain, workload, status, accreditation, adoption_stage, maturity_score, TRL, source — no health-outcome, wellbeing, or population-impact field anywhere in the schema; regulations.json (99 rows) has no recourse/redress field

**Observation:** The procurement record measures the technical maturity of government health-data systems in detail over the same populations and years in which outcome statistics deteriorated and recovered, yet contains no field in which a health outcome could even be recorded.

*Basis:* structural

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show any deployment affected suicide, overdose, or any health outcome. The absence of outcome fields is a property of what the record measures, not evidence of harm or benefit.

### Pandemic-era mental health elevated: WHO 25% global rise in anxiety/depression first pandemic year (2022-03-02); US adult PHQ-8 depression 18.5% (2019) → 21.4% (2022) (NHSR 213)
[A] temporal

**Gov Cloud fact:** deployments.json: 10 of 14 pandemic-response deployments decommissioned (3 production, 1 accredited); milestones.json: COVIDSafe deleted 2022-08-10; EU DCC regulation lapsed 2023-06-30; HHS Tiberius wound down; CDC VAMS abandoned by most states

**Observation:** The emergency pandemic data infrastructure was largely dismantled across 2022-2023, during the same period pandemic-era mental-health indicators remained elevated above pre-pandemic baselines into 2022.

*Basis:* structural

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show decommissioning caused, prolonged, or relieved distress, nor that retaining these systems would have changed any indicator. The systems tracked infection, contact and vaccination — not mental health.

### US suicide rise 1999-2018 occurred in the WHO Americas region while most other regions declined
[A] jurisdictional

**Gov Cloud fact:** geographies.json: 6 of 35 jurisdictions in the americas region (US, US-CO, CA, BR, CL, MX); deployments.json: the US holds 7 of 32 health-domain deployments — the most of any single jurisdiction, all in production (NIH STRIDES x3, CMS Hybrid Cloud x2, VA x2)

**Observation:** The jurisdiction with the densest health-cloud deployment coverage in the dataset (US) is also the jurisdiction whose suicide-rate rise is documented in the register's health-signal corpus.

*Basis:* structural

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show any relation between US health-cloud deployments and suicide rates. The rise began in 1999, before any deployment in this dataset; co-location reflects US documentation practices.

### Psychiatric prescribing rising in England 2016-2025 (NHSBSA) and the US (ASPE/IQVIA), while schizophrenia prevalence stable (GBD)
[B] both

**Gov Cloud fact:** milestones.json: NHS England direct award of the Federated Data Platform to Palantir 2023-11-21 (GBP330M/7yr), pre-action legal challenge 2023-11-30; deployments.json: GB has 4 health-domain deployments, all production

**Observation:** England's largest health-data platform procurement (FDP, 2023) occurred midway through a documented decade of rising psychiatric prescribing in the same health system.

*Basis:* pattern

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show the FDP relates to prescribing volumes in any direction. The prescribing rise began ~7 years before the FDP award; no prescribing-effect evidence exists in either corpus.

### 2022 was the record year for both US overdose deaths (107,941; db549) and US suicides (49,476; db509)
[B] both

**Gov Cloud fact:** deployments.json: CDC disease monitoring (DCIPHER/HHS Protect lineage) expanded 2022 — Palantir, FedRAMP High, production; one of only 3 pandemic-response systems still in production

**Observation:** The CDC's cloud disease-monitoring platform was expanded in the same year the US recorded its highest-ever overdose and suicide death counts.

*Basis:* pattern

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show the expansion affected either death count, or that the deaths motivated the expansion. DCIPHER monitors infectious disease; the co-occurrence is calendar-year only.

### US life expectancy dipped 2020-21 and recovered to 79.0 by 2024 (db548)
[B] temporal

**Gov Cloud fact:** milestones.json: Tiberius live 2020-08-01, VAMS live 2020-12-01, COVIDSafe launched 2020-04-26 (~6-week emergency build); 10 of 14 pandemic systems decommissioned by ~2022-2023

**Observation:** The full lifecycle of the emergency data infrastructure — built in months during 2020, largely torn down by 2023 — brackets the US life-expectancy dip; the return to 79.0 by 2024 post-dates the teardown.

*Basis:* structural

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show the systems shortened or lengthened the mortality dip, nor that their removal enabled or delayed recovery. Both timelines are driven by the pandemic itself; the alignment is definitional, not evidential.

### US fentanyl wave onset 2013 (CDC); overdose deaths then rose to the 2022 record
[C] temporal

**Gov Cloud fact:** regulations.json: dataset's regulatory era begins with FedRAMP (2011), FISMA modernization (2014); milestones.json health/pandemic entries begin 2019-02-06; deployments.json contains no date fields — timing recoverable only through milestones

**Observation:** The deadliest documented US drug-supply shift (2013) predates nearly all health-domain cloud infrastructure recorded in this dataset (health milestones begin 2019) — the register also records where a health signal precedes the infrastructure entirely.

*Basis:* pattern

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show absence of infrastructure contributed to the epidemic, nor that later infrastructure responded to it. Included to demonstrate temporal precedence runs in both directions.

### Psychiatric prescribing rising 2016-2025 while schizophrenia prevalence stable (GBD)
[A] temporal

**Gov Cloud fact:** regulations.json: 8 of 99 instruments flag neural_data — OECD neurotech recommendation (2019), Chile Law 21.383 (2021), Chile Supreme Court Girardi v. Emotiv (2023), California SB 1223 (2024), Colorado HB24-1058 (2024), Montana SB 163 (2025), UNESCO recommendation (2025), UK ICO strategy (2026, proposed); 0 of 99 record any recourse mechanism

**Observation:** The period of rising psychiatric prescribing (2016-2025) is also the period in which jurisdictions began writing brain-data collection rules (2019-2026); the regulation record captures what may be collected but has no field for what a person can do about it.

*Basis:* structural

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show any link between neural-data regulation and prescribing trends, or between either and brain health. Records the co-timing of two documentation waves and a structural gap in the regulatory record.

### Pandemic-era distress indicators remained elevated into 2022 (NHSR 213; WHO 2022-03-02)
[B] temporal

**Gov Cloud fact:** milestones.json: Aotearoa Immunisation Register made permanent 2022-11-01 ('coevolution': pandemic register hardened into permanent NIR replacement); NZ CIR and COVID Tracer decommissioned

**Observation:** While most pandemic systems were dismantled, at least one (NZ's immunisation register) was made permanent in late 2022 — the same period distress indicators remained elevated — the infrastructure's fate diverged (teardown vs permanence) with no reference to health-indicator trajectories in either case.

*Basis:* pattern

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show the register's permanence relates to mental-health indicators anywhere. The US/WHO indicators cited are not NZ-specific.

### The register's verified health signals come from US (CDC/NCHS), England (NHSBSA), and global (WHO/GBD) statistical systems, 1999-2025
[A] jurisdictional

**Gov Cloud fact:** deployments.json: health deployments span 12 of 35 jurisdictions — US 7, GB 4, CN 3, DE 3, EU 3, RU 3, FR 2, IL 2, NZ 2, AE 1, AU 1, QA 1

**Observation:** The overlap register can only be dense where both corpora are dense: the US and UK account for 11 of 32 health deployments and nearly all citable outcome statistics; most dataset jurisdictions (incl. CN, RU, AE) have health deployments but no comparable outcome series to overlap against.

*Basis:* structural

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show health outcomes differ by deployment density. Documents a coverage artifact: where statistics and procurement records are co-published, overlaps become visible; elsewhere they cannot be constructed at all.

### US overdose deaths declined from the 2022 record to 79,384 in 2024 (−26.2%) and provisional 69,973 in 2025
[C] both

**Gov Cloud fact:** milestones.json (track E): BARDA FY2025 enacted $1.015B with FY2026 request $654M, declining; total US biodefense FY2026 request declining across agencies

**Observation:** US overdose deaths and US federal biodefense/pandemic-preparedness budgets declined over the same 2023-2026 window.

*Basis:* pattern

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show any relation between the two declines — biodefense funding does not address overdose; the overdose decline is attributed elsewhere (naloxone access, supply changes). Recorded strictly as a co-trend.

### Mental-health indicators remained above pre-pandemic baselines into 2022, the period pandemic credentials were wound down
[B] temporal

**Gov Cloud fact:** milestones.json: WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network adopted the EU DCC standard globally 2023-06-05 ('coevolution', 'standard persists'), 25 days before the EU DCC regulation lapsed 2023-06-30 ('decoupled')

**Observation:** The legal instrument behind Europe's pandemic credential expired in June 2023, but its technical standard had been globalized by the WHO weeks earlier — the infrastructure pattern outlived its legal basis during the tail of the pandemic-era mental-health elevation.

*Basis:* structural

*Not a causal claim:* Does not show certification infrastructure affected mental health in any way, nor that its persistence or lapse had health consequences.

# What the series show

*Independent research compiled from public records for informational purposes only. Not legal, medical, or investment advice. Evidence tiers: **A** documented, **B** corroborated, **C** claimed — B and C may not be quoted as established fact. Causes are reported as attributed, never asserted. This dataset does not corroborate, and is not corroborated by, any other dataset in this corpus. See `meta/IS_META_terms.md`.*

One sourced statement per series.

**31 entries.**

- [A] **Global decline 2000-2019** — Global age-standardized suicide rate fell 36% 2000-2019 (WHO); GHE values: 12.51 (2000) -> 9.42 (2019) -> 9.13 (2021). — World Health Organization · One in 100 deaths is by suicide (launch of 'Suicide worldwide in 2019') <https://www.who.int/news/item/17-06-2021-one-in-100-deaths-is-by-suicide>

- [A] **Regional divergence — Americas rose** — 2000-2019 rates fell in five WHO regions (17% E. Mediterranean to 47% Europe, 49% W. Pacific) but 'in the Americas Region, rates increased by 17%' (WHO). — World Health Organization · One in 100 deaths is by suicide (launch of 'Suicide worldwide in 2019') <https://www.who.int/news/item/17-06-2021-one-in-100-deaths-is-by-suicide>

- [A] **China — one of the world's largest declines** — From adjusted 23/100k in 1995-99 (~287,000 deaths/yr) to WHO GHE 8.75 in 2019; 1987-2020 registration analysis: urban ASR down ~66%, rural ~81%; historical female excess reversed after 2005. — BMC Public Health · Long-term changing patterns of suicide mortality in China 1987-2020 <https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12889-024-18743-z>

- [A] **Russia — steep decline from world-leading levels** — WHO-estimated rate fell 53.06 (2000) -> 24.47 (2019) -> 21.37 (2021); 2006 alcohol policy attributed 'an immediate and permanent reduction of about 9%' in male suicide mortality (~4,000 male lives/yr), no detected female effect (AJPH 2013). — AJPH via PMC · Pridemore et al. — 2006 Russian Alcohol Policy and Male Suicide Mortality <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3828708/>

- [A] **Russia — official decline partly overstated** — Undetermined-intent deaths declined far more slowly than coded suicides; true mortality likely exceeds Rosstat by ~60% (M) / >2x (F) — part of the recorded decline is coding migration, not fewer deaths. — European Journal of Public Health · Semyonova et al. — Russian suicide mortality: official and actual rates <https://academic.oup.com/eurpub/article/30/Supplement_5/ckaa166.1371/5915576>

- [B] **India — rising recorded counts vs flat-declining modeled rate** — NCRB record 170,924 (2022; 12.4/lakh, up from 9.9 in 2017) — highest in 56 yrs of ADSI — while WHO GHE modeled rates declined (15.93 in 2000 -> 12.56 in 2021). Part of the recorded rise plausibly reflects improving reporting against a large historical undercount. — CMHLP · Takeaways from the NCRB data on suicide for 2022 <https://cmhlp.org/imho/blog/takeaways-from-the-ncrb-data-on-suicide-for-2022/>

- [A] **Global undercount as first-class finding** — Peer-reviewed meta-analysis: 17.9% of suicides missing from official statistics worldwide — implying >1 million actual deaths/yr vs WHO's ~727,000 — concentrated in LMICs incl. India and China (34.9%). — Frontiers in Psychiatry · Meda et al. — How many people die by suicide each year? Not 727,000 <https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychiatry/articles/10.3389/fpsyt.2025.1609580/full>

- [A] **cancer_incidence_overall** — US age-adjusted incidence (all sites) stable 2013-2022 (~445.8/100k), but aggregate masks divergence: rising in women and several sites (breast, prostate, pancreas, liver in women, melanoma, oral cavity, uterine corpus) while falling/stable in others. — NCI SEER · Cancer Stat Facts: Cancer of Any Site <https://seer.cancer.gov/statfacts/html/all.html>

- [A] **cancer_mortality** — US cancer mortality falling, not rising: death rate down 34% from 1991 peak through 2023 (~4.8M deaths averted), −1.5%/yr 2014-2023, 5-yr relative survival 70%. — American Cancer Society · Annual Cancer Statistics Report 2026 <https://pressroom.cancer.org/cancer-statistics-report-2026>

- [A] **early_onset_cancer** — Globally, new cancer cases under 50 rose 79% 1990-2019 (3.26M in 2019) while early-onset deaths rose only 28% — incidence rising much faster than mortality. — BMJ Group (BMJ Oncology) · Global surge in cancers among the under 50s over past three decades <https://bmjgroup.com/global-surge-in-cancers-among-the-under-50s-over-past-three-decades/>

- [A] **early_onset_cancer_us** — US cancer incidence in women <50 now 82% higher than men <50 (up from 51% in 2002); colorectal incidence rising ~3%/yr ages 20-49 while falling 2.5%/yr in 65+. — American Cancer Society · ACS Annual Report 2025: Cancer Mortality Continues to Drop Despite Rising Incidence in Women <https://pressroom.cancer.org/2025CancerFactsandFigures>

- [A] **depression_us** — Multiple independent US measures show depression rising over the last decade: PHQ-8 symptoms 18.5% (2019) → 21.4% (2022) per NCHS/NHIS; Gallup ever-diagnosed 20.6% (2017) → 29.0% (2023); steepest among 18-29s and women. — CDC/NCHS · Symptoms of Anxiety and Depression Among Adults: United States, 2019 and 2022 (NHSR 213) <https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/nhsr/nhsr213.pdf>

- [B] **depression_counterpoint** — Counterpoint: 2024 NSDUH shows adolescent past-year MDE fell 18.1% (2023) → 15.4% (2024); adult SMI roughly flat (5.7% → 5.6%) — recent official data do not show a continuing monotonic rise. — NACo (citing SAMHSA 2024 NSDUH) · SAMHSA releases new 2024 data on rates of mental illness and substance use disorder <https://www.naco.org/news/samhsa-releases-new-2024-data-rates-mental-illness-and-substance-use-disorder-us>

- [A] **anxiety** — US adult anxiety symptoms (GAD-7) rose 15.6% (2019) → 18.2% (2022), ages 18-29 19.5% → 26.6% (NCHS/NHIS); WHO estimated a 25% global increase in anxiety and depression in the first pandemic year; anxiety disorders 359M people (4.4%) in 2021. — WHO · COVID-19 pandemic triggers 25% increase in prevalence of anxiety and depression worldwide <https://www.who.int/news/item/02-03-2022-covid-19-pandemic-triggers-25-increase-in-prevalence-of-anxiety-and-depression-worldwide>

- [A] **drug_overdose** — US overdose deaths peaked at 107,941 (2022, rate 32.6), fell to 105,007 (2023) and 79,384 (2024, −26.2%, largest one-year decline of 2014-2024), provisional 2025 ~69,973 (−14%, third consecutive annual decline). A major documented counterpoint to a worsening-overdose narrative. — CDC/NCHS · Drug Overdose Deaths in the United States, 2023-2024 (Data Brief 549, Jan 2026) <https://cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db549.htm>

- [A] **life_expectancy** — US life expectancy flat 2014-2019 (78.9→78.8), fell to 77.0 (2020) and 76.4 (2021), recovered to 77.5 (2022), 78.4 (2023), 79.0 (2024) — above pre-pandemic. Still trails peer average (82.7 in 2024; 3.7-yr gap), a divergence that widened through the 2010s and pandemic and narrowed slightly 2023-2024. — CDC/NCHS · Mortality in the United States, 2024 (Data Brief 548, Jan 2026) <https://cdc.gov/nchs/products/databriefs/db548.htm>

- [A] **schizophrenia_prevalence** — Consensus: point prevalence low and stable — GBD 2016 global age-standardised 0.28% (UI 0.24-0.31), age-specific prevalence 'largely consistent over time and across countries'; case growth (13.1m 1990 -> 20.9m 2016) driven by population growth/ageing. — Schizophrenia Bulletin · Charlson et al., Global Epidemiology and Burden of Schizophrenia (GBD 2016) <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6192504/>

- [A] **schizophrenia_prevalence** — GBD 2021: prevalent cases +70.1% (13.62m -> 23.18m 1990-2021) but age-standardised prevalence 'relatively stable', incidence slightly declining (EAPC -0.04) — no epidemic of new disease. — Frontiers in Psychiatry · GBD schizophrenia trends 1990-2021 and projections to 2050 <https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychiatry/articles/10.3389/fpsyt.2025.1629032/full>

- [A] **schizophrenia_prevalence** — NIMH: US prevalence of schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders 0.25%-0.64%; international 0.33%-0.75% — consistent with the ~0.3-0.7% consensus band. — NIMH · Schizophrenia — statistics <https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/statistics/schizophrenia>

- [A] **schizophrenia_diagnoses** — Denmark national registry 2000-2018: diagnosed schizophrenia incidence did NOT rise (1.8 -> 1.6 per 10,000); schizotypal diagnoses nearly doubled — shifts in diagnostic practice within the spectrum, not rising schizophrenia. — Acta Psychiatrica Scandinavica · Köhler-Forsberg et al., Schizophrenia spectrum disorders in Denmark 2000-2018 <https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/acps.13565>

- [A] **antipsychotic_prescribing_vs_diagnosis** — Antipsychotic items in England rose 146% (4.71m 1998 -> 11.62m 2022; +111% per capita) 'despite stable estimated prevalence of psychotic disorders' — prescribing volume and diagnosis prevalence have decoupled. — BJPsych Open · Newman et al., Twenty-five year trend in antipsychotic prescribing in England (2025) <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12303834/>

- [A] **antipsychotic_prescribing_england** — NHSBSA: antipsychotic items 11.0m (2015/16) -> 13.2m (2021/22, +19.7%) -> 13.9m items / 873,000 patients (2024/25); recent year-on-year growth under 1% (Q3 2024/25). — NHSBSA (open data) · MUMH annual summary 2015/16 to 2021/22 <https://nhsbsa-opendata.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/mumh/mumh_annual_2021_22_v002.html>

- [B] **antipsychotic_treated_prevalence_hk** — Hong Kong 11-year population study of 62,607 schizophrenia-spectrum patients (2011-2021, joinpoint regression; J Psychiatr Res 2025, PMID 39961232, DOI 10.1016/j.jpsychires.2025.02.017) documents territory-wide utilization trends. NOTE: abstract figures could not be retrieved this session (all mirrors blocked) — pull exact figures from the paper before quoting numbers. — J Psychiatric Research (PubMed record) · Hong Kong 11-year antipsychotic utilization study (DOI 10.1016/j.jpsychires.2025.02.017) <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39961232/>

- [A] **antidepressant_prescribing_england** — Antidepressant items rose every year on record: 61.9m (2015/16) -> 83.4m (2021/22) -> 92.6m (2024/25), 8.89m patients — ~50% volume increase in nine years. — NHSBSA · Medicines Used in Mental Health – England – 2015/16 to 2024/25 <https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/statistical-collections/medicines-used-mental-health-england/medicines-used-mental-health-england-201516-202425>

- [B] **antidepressant_prescribing_us_youth** — US antidepressant dispensing to adolescents/young adults (IQVIA ~92% of pharmacies, 2016-2022) rose 63.5% faster after March 2020 than pre-pandemic trend — +130% among female adolescents — while male adolescent dispensing declined (Chua et al., Pediatrics 2024). — U. Michigan IHPI · Antidepressant dispensing to adolescents surges during pandemic <https://ihpi.umich.edu/news-events/news/antidepressant-dispensing-adolescents-and-young-adults-surges-during-pandemic>

- [A] **adhd_stimulant_prescribing_us** — US stimulant prescriptions +60% 2012-2023 (50.4m -> 80.8m), accelerating after 2020; women +92% vs men +36%; ages 31-40 +240% (DEA/IQVIA, Nov 2024). — IQVIA for DEA · Stimulant Prescription Trends in the United States, 2012-2023 <https://www.deadiversion.usdoj.gov/pubs/docs/IQVIA-Report-on-Stimulant-Trends-2024.pdf>

- [A] **adhd_stimulant_prescribing_us** — Commercially insured 5-64 with >=1 stimulant fill: 3.6% (2016) -> 4.1% (2021), with 2020->2021 jumps ~14-19% among adult women and men 25-44 (CDC MMWR 2023). — CDC MMWR · Danielson et al., Trends in Stimulant Prescription Fills 2016-2021 <https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/wr/mm7213a1.htm>

- [A] **adhd_prescribing_england** — CNS stimulant/ADHD items in England more than doubled 1.31m (2015/16) -> 3.38m (2024/25); adults prescribed rose 24.3% in one year to 190,000. — NHSBSA · Medicines Used in Mental Health – England – 2015/16 to 2024/25 <https://www.nhsbsa.nhs.uk/statistical-collections/medicines-used-mental-health-england/medicines-used-mental-health-england-201516-202425>

- [A] **benzodiazepine_prescribing** — Benzodiazepines run counter: England hypnotic/anxiolytic items FELL 12% (15.9m 2015/16 -> 14.0m 2021/22; 13.4m 2024/25); US adults 65+ fell 14.1 -> 11.5 per 100 (2015-2024), declining pre-pandemic then plateauing. — NHSBSA (open data) · MUMH annual summary 2015/16 to 2021/22 <https://nhsbsa-opendata.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com/mumh/mumh_annual_2021_22_v002.html>

- [A] **antipsychotic_use_us** — US adult antipsychotic use rose 1.9% (2006) -> 3.0% (2023) of adults — several times the ~0.3-0.6% schizophrenia prevalence, confirming most volume is prescribed for other conditions; youth use slightly declined (1.3% -> 1.1%). — HHS ASPE · US Population Prevalence of Psychotropic Medication Use, 2006-2023 <https://www.aspe.hhs.gov/sites/default/files/documents/1ef68c455fa5aa5932acf481b0954ddf/DataPoint_PsychRxPrev_BHDAP_20250409%20July%2031%202025.pdf>

- [A] **drug_overdose** — US overdose deaths rose from 16,849 in 1999 (rate 6.1) to 107,941 in 2022 (rate 32.6) — a 541% increase in the count over twenty-three years, with the steepest acceleration after 2013 and the largest single-year rise in 2020 (+30.0%). The post-2022 decline runs down from that peak, not from the pre-2000 baseline: provisional 2025 (69,973) is still about four times the 1999 count. — CDC/NCHS · Data tables for NCHS Data Brief 428: Drug Overdose Deaths in the United States, 1999-2020 <https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/databriefs/db428-tables.pdf>

basis,govcloud_fact,health_signal,non_causal_note,observation,overlap_id,overlap_type,tier
structural,"deployments.json (399 rows, health=32, 29 production) records only id, geography, vendor, domain, workload, status, accreditation, adoption_stage, maturity_score, TRL, source — no health-outcome, wellbeing, or population-impact field anywhere in the schema; regulations.json (99 rows) has no recourse/redress field","US suicide rate rose ~30-35% 1999-2018 (CDC MMWR mm6722a1; NCHS db362); record 49,476 deaths 2022 (db509); overdose record 107,941 in 2022 (db549)","Does not show any deployment affected suicide, overdose, or any health outcome. The absence of outcome fields is a property of what the record measures, not evidence of harm or benefit.","The procurement record measures the technical maturity of government health-data systems in detail over the same populations and years in which outcome statistics deteriorated and recovered, yet contains no field in which a health outcome could even be recorded.",ov01,both,A
structural,"deployments.json: 10 of 14 pandemic-response deployments decommissioned (3 production, 1 accredited); milestones.json: COVIDSafe deleted 2022-08-10; EU DCC regulation lapsed 2023-06-30; HHS Tiberius wound down; CDC VAMS abandoned by most states",Pandemic-era mental health elevated: WHO 25% global rise in anxiety/depression first pandemic year (2022-03-02); US adult PHQ-8 depression 18.5% (2019) → 21.4% (2022) (NHSR 213),"Does not show decommissioning caused, prolonged, or relieved distress, nor that retaining these systems would have changed any indicator. The systems tracked infection, contact and vaccination — not mental health.","The emergency pandemic data infrastructure was largely dismantled across 2022-2023, during the same period pandemic-era mental-health indicators remained elevated above pre-pandemic baselines into 2022.",ov02,temporal,A
structural,"geographies.json: 6 of 35 jurisdictions in the americas region (US, US-CO, CA, BR, CL, MX); deployments.json: the US holds 7 of 32 health-domain deployments — the most of any single jurisdiction, all in production (NIH STRIDES x3, CMS Hybrid Cloud x2, VA x2)",US suicide rise 1999-2018 occurred in the WHO Americas region while most other regions declined,"Does not show any relation between US health-cloud deployments and suicide rates. The rise began in 1999, before any deployment in this dataset; co-location reflects US documentation practices.",The jurisdiction with the densest health-cloud deployment coverage in the dataset (US) is also the jurisdiction whose suicide-rate rise is documented in the register's health-signal corpus.,ov03,jurisdictional,A
pattern,"milestones.json: NHS England direct award of the Federated Data Platform to Palantir 2023-11-21 (GBP330M/7yr), pre-action legal challenge 2023-11-30; deployments.json: GB has 4 health-domain deployments, all production","Psychiatric prescribing rising in England 2016-2025 (NHSBSA) and the US (ASPE/IQVIA), while schizophrenia prevalence stable (GBD)",Does not show the FDP relates to prescribing volumes in any direction. The prescribing rise began ~7 years before the FDP award; no prescribing-effect evidence exists in either corpus.,"England's largest health-data platform procurement (FDP, 2023) occurred midway through a documented decade of rising psychiatric prescribing in the same health system.",ov04,both,B
pattern,"deployments.json: CDC disease monitoring (DCIPHER/HHS Protect lineage) expanded 2022 — Palantir, FedRAMP High, production; one of only 3 pandemic-response systems still in production","2022 was the record year for both US overdose deaths (107,941; db549) and US suicides (49,476; db509)","Does not show the expansion affected either death count, or that the deaths motivated the expansion. DCIPHER monitors infectious disease; the co-occurrence is calendar-year only.",The CDC's cloud disease-monitoring platform was expanded in the same year the US recorded its highest-ever overdose and suicide death counts.,ov05,both,B
structural,"milestones.json: Tiberius live 2020-08-01, VAMS live 2020-12-01, COVIDSafe launched 2020-04-26 (~6-week emergency build); 10 of 14 pandemic systems decommissioned by ~2022-2023",US life expectancy dipped 2020-21 and recovered to 79.0 by 2024 (db548),"Does not show the systems shortened or lengthened the mortality dip, nor that their removal enabled or delayed recovery. Both timelines are driven by the pandemic itself; the alignment is definitional, not evidential.","The full lifecycle of the emergency data infrastructure — built in months during 2020, largely torn down by 2023 — brackets the US life-expectancy dip; the return to 79.0 by 2024 post-dates the teardown.",ov06,temporal,B
pattern,"regulations.json: dataset's regulatory era begins with FedRAMP (2011), FISMA modernization (2014); milestones.json health/pandemic entries begin 2019-02-06; deployments.json contains no date fields — timing recoverable only through milestones",US fentanyl wave onset 2013 (CDC); overdose deaths then rose to the 2022 record,"Does not show absence of infrastructure contributed to the epidemic, nor that later infrastructure responded to it. Included to demonstrate temporal precedence runs in both directions.",The deadliest documented US drug-supply shift (2013) predates nearly all health-domain cloud infrastructure recorded in this dataset (health milestones begin 2019) — the register also records where a health signal precedes the infrastructure entirely.,ov07,temporal,C
structural,"regulations.json: 8 of 99 instruments flag neural_data — OECD neurotech recommendation (2019), Chile Law 21.383 (2021), Chile Supreme Court Girardi v. Emotiv (2023), California SB 1223 (2024), Colorado HB24-1058 (2024), Montana SB 163 (2025), UNESCO recommendation (2025), UK ICO strategy (2026, proposed); 0 of 99 record any recourse mechanism",Psychiatric prescribing rising 2016-2025 while schizophrenia prevalence stable (GBD),"Does not show any link between neural-data regulation and prescribing trends, or between either and brain health. Records the co-timing of two documentation waves and a structural gap in the regulatory record.",The period of rising psychiatric prescribing (2016-2025) is also the period in which jurisdictions began writing brain-data collection rules (2019-2026); the regulation record captures what may be collected but has no field for what a person can do about it.,ov08,temporal,A
pattern,milestones.json: Aotearoa Immunisation Register made permanent 2022-11-01 ('coevolution': pandemic register hardened into permanent NIR replacement); NZ CIR and COVID Tracer decommissioned,Pandemic-era distress indicators remained elevated into 2022 (NHSR 213; WHO 2022-03-02),Does not show the register's permanence relates to mental-health indicators anywhere. The US/WHO indicators cited are not NZ-specific.,"While most pandemic systems were dismantled, at least one (NZ's immunisation register) was made permanent in late 2022 — the same period distress indicators remained elevated — the infrastructure's fate diverged (teardown vs permanence) with no reference to health-indicator trajectories in either case.",ov09,temporal,B
structural,"deployments.json: health deployments span 12 of 35 jurisdictions — US 7, GB 4, CN 3, DE 3, EU 3, RU 3, FR 2, IL 2, NZ 2, AE 1, AU 1, QA 1","The register's verified health signals come from US (CDC/NCHS), England (NHSBSA), and global (WHO/GBD) statistical systems, 1999-2025","Does not show health outcomes differ by deployment density. Documents a coverage artifact: where statistics and procurement records are co-published, overlaps become visible; elsewhere they cannot be constructed at all.","The overlap register can only be dense where both corpora are dense: the US and UK account for 11 of 32 health deployments and nearly all citable outcome statistics; most dataset jurisdictions (incl. CN, RU, AE) have health deployments but no comparable outcome series to overlap against.",ov10,jurisdictional,A
pattern,"milestones.json (track E): BARDA FY2025 enacted $1.015B with FY2026 request $654M, declining; total US biodefense FY2026 request declining across agencies","US overdose deaths declined from the 2022 record to 79,384 in 2024 (−26.2%) and provisional 69,973 in 2025","Does not show any relation between the two declines — biodefense funding does not address overdose; the overdose decline is attributed elsewhere (naloxone access, supply changes). Recorded strictly as a co-trend.",US overdose deaths and US federal biodefense/pandemic-preparedness budgets declined over the same 2023-2026 window.,ov11,both,C
structural,"milestones.json: WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network adopted the EU DCC standard globally 2023-06-05 ('coevolution', 'standard persists'), 25 days before the EU DCC regulation lapsed 2023-06-30 ('decoupled')","Mental-health indicators remained above pre-pandemic baselines into 2022, the period pandemic credentials were wound down","Does not show certification infrastructure affected mental health in any way, nor that its persistence or lapse had health consequences.","The legal instrument behind Europe's pandemic credential expired in June 2023, but its technical standard had been globalized by the WHO weeks earlier — the infrastructure pattern outlived its legal basis during the tail of the pandemic-era mental-health elevation.",ov12,temporal,B

# Government Cloud Research — Web Data Package (Next.js + d3.js)

Drop this folder into your Next.js app at `public/data/` and fetch the JSON, or `import` it directly.

## Layout
- `tables/*.json` — the 11 dataset tables as record arrays (mirror the Supabase schema; see `../03-dataset/sql/migration.sql`).
- `charts/*.json` — pre-shaped, d3-ready datasets so charts need no client-side aggregation.
- `types.ts` — TypeScript interfaces for every table and chart shape. Copy into `lib/` or `types/`.
- `manifest.json` — index + row counts + paths.

## Two ways to use
1. **Static (simplest):** copy to `public/data/`, then `const d = await fetch('/data/charts/timeline.json').then(r=>r.json())`.
2. **Supabase (live):** apply `../03-dataset/sql/migration.sql` + `seed.sql`, then query via `@supabase/supabase-js`. The `*_sourced` SQL views expose the source URL + tier on every fact row. Regenerate these JSONs any time from the CSVs.

## d3 chart → data file map
- Master timeline (5 tracks) → `charts/timeline.json` (each point has numeric `year` for the x-scale; `track` A–E for the lane; `certainty` for hollow/filled).
- Geo × domain heatmap → `charts/geo_domain_matrix.json`.
- Vendor ranking (bar) → `charts/vendor_deploy_rank.json`.
- Funding → vendor → geography **Sankey** → `charts/sankey_funding.json` (`{nodes,links}`, ready for `d3-sankey`).
- Award value by geography / by year / re-compete → `charts/awards_*.json`, `charts/recompete.json`.
- Capital flows (disclosed vs pledge), market size, thesis → `charts/capital_flows.json`, `market_size_by_domain.json`, `investment_thesis.json`.
- Litigation by vendor/status/jurisdiction + register → `charts/litigation_*.json`.
- Capabilities by category/vendor + register → `charts/capabilities_*.json`.

## Evidence-tier rule (important)
Every fact carries a `tier` (A/B/C). For any public-facing view, filter or visibly mark Tier C
(claimed/theoretical). Keep documented (A) separate from alleged (C) — this is what the report's
credibility rests on.

## Palette (matches the delivered dashboard, validated for light+dark, CVD-safe)
series-1 `#2a78d6` · series-2 `#eb6834` · series-3 `#1baf7a` · series-4 `#eda100` · series-5 `#4a3aa7`
(dark: `#3987e5 #d95926 #199e70 #c98500 #9085e9`). Timeline tracks: A=2, B=1, C=3, D=4, E=5.

# Government Cloud Research — Challenge, Position & Calls to Action

*Consolidated across all six research layers · 2026-08-17 · informational only, not legal or
investment advice.*

## The Challenge (the problem this report confronts)

**The infrastructure that now runs the world's governments — cloud, AI, biometric identity,
data-fusion and surveillance platforms — is being deployed faster than any of the systems meant
to govern it can keep up, and no one has been able to see the whole board at once.** Adoption,
procurement money, sovereignty law, capability, capital, and litigation have each been reported
in isolation, so the public, journalists, oversight bodies, and even the buyers themselves lack
a single, sourced, evidence-tiered picture of *who runs what government workload, on whose
platform, under what law, funded by whom, doing what, and contested in which court.* Without
that unified picture, three failures follow: governments regulate after deployment instead of
before; the public cannot tell documented fact from marketing or conspiracy; and the harms —
wrongful arrests, unlawful surveillance, uncollected privacy fines — recur unmeasured.

**This project is the answer to that challenge:** one auditable, source-cited, tier-labeled
dataset and dashboard that puts all six dimensions on the same board — so the picture can be
seen, questioned, and acted on. The remaining task is to publish it without letting the framing
outrun the evidence.

## Position in one paragraph

The research plan is complete and extended. What began as a four-prompt plan (adoption,
procurement, regulation, timeline) now spans **six layers plus a timeline that weaves them
together**, in an eleven-table dataset that reproduces in Supabase from one `seed.sql`:
**399 deployments · 90 awards · 99 regulations · 311 timeline milestones (5 threads) · 81
investment rows · 46 lawsuits · 73 platform capabilities · 660 sources · 34 geographies.** A
six-view dashboard renders all of it. Every fact carries a source and an evidence tier;
documented (Tier A) is held apart from reported (B) and claimed (C) throughout. What remains
is not research — it is the pre-publication hardening.

## The five findings the whole body of work converges on

1. **Sovereignty law is now the binding constraint on government cloud** — 44 of 99
   instruments compel localisation or domestic control, and **EU–US data adequacy (the Latombe
   case at the CJEU) is the single highest-leverage failure point** across the entire dataset.
2. **Law follows capability, not the reverse** — 16 milestones classify as law-following vs 4
   capability-following; governments regulate these systems after they are already deployed.
3. **The money is bimodal and must not be summed** — ~$1.46T disclosed vs ~$868B in announced
   pledges; the bankable value is disclosed revenue/appropriations, not Gulf mega-pledges.
4. **Litigation is a primary market force** — it reversed a $10B procurement (JEDI), banned a
   technology (Rite Aid), forced transparency (NHS), and created a neural-data right (Girardi);
   Clearview alone is litigated 15 times with fines largely uncollected.
5. **Enforcement output is policy-driven, not technology-driven** — the 2025 sequence shows the
   policy switch preceding the software and the appropriations; the tech is a throughput
   multiplier, carried with its documented error-and-harm tail.

## Calls to action — by audience

The report speaks to five audiences; each has its own "so what, do this."

- **The publisher (you):** publish the documented board, keep the tiers visible, get counsel on
  named parties — then let the data speak. Your CTA is section A below.
- **Policymakers & oversight bodies:** close the pacing gap where government already operates in
  it — biometric and neuro-adjacent workloads run live under a patchwork with a government
  carve-out (Colorado). Instrument the harm; the error-and-harm tail is real and unmeasured.
- **Vendors & procurement leads:** the 2028 re-compete wave is scoped in 2026–27, and EU–US
  adequacy is the portfolio's dominant risk. Architect for a Schrems-III world now, not after.
- **Investors:** anchor on the disclosed column ($1.46T), not the pledges ($868B); the
  actionable signal is the per-domain thesis divergence (govtech + sensing-fusion high;
  neurotech capital-ahead-of-returns; neuro-forensics nothing to size).
- **Journalists, researchers & civil society:** the capability register and the litigation
  register describe the same tools from two angles — what they do, and what they've been sued
  over. That pairing is the investigative lead.

## Call to action — decision-forcing (execution sequence)

**A. Do the pre-publication hardening before invisibleships.com goes live.** *(This is the
live decision.)*
- **Legal/counsel review** — the report names companies and individuals; the publisher carries
  defamation exposure. Owner: you + counsel. Window: before posting. Cost of inaction: a single
  named-party complaint can force takedown and discredit the whole work.
- **Preserve the tier labels and keep documented separate from alleged** on the live site (the
  dashboard already supports this). Owner: you. Cost of inaction: a hostile reader dismisses the
  entire report on its weakest Tier-C line.
- **Wayback capture of all 660 sources** (`archived_url` still empty). Owner: me, next session.
  Cost of inaction: link rot makes citations unverifiable exactly when scrutiny is highest.

**B. Ship the master synthesis + neuro-ethics grounding chapter.** The six briefs exist; a
single executive report with the disclaimer front-matter and the required neuroscience/
neuro-ethics chapter does not yet. Owner: me. Window: next session. This is what makes it read
as one authored report rather than six research outputs.

**C. Stand up the live site on the real data.** The data is now prepped for your stack:
`04-site/webdata/` (also delivered as `gov-cloud-webdata.zip`) has all 11 tables + 17 d3-ready
chart files + a funding→vendor→geography Sankey + `types.ts` + `manifest.json` + a README.
Drop it into Next.js at `public/data/` (static), or query Supabase live (migration.sql +
seed.sql ready; `*_sourced` views carry source URL + tier per row). d3 charts map 1:1 to the
chart files (see README). Owner: you/dev. Window: after hardening (A).

**D. Set the watchlist to run.** Prompt 3's indicators (the Latombe ruling, AI-Act deadlines,
neural-data enforcement, re-compete dates) convert into a scheduled monitoring task so the
dataset stays live rather than a snapshot. Owner: me, on request.

**Watch, don't act yet:** the EU AI Act high-risk deadlines and the Gulf AI-compute dollar
headlines — both are contested/soft and will move; don't build conclusions on them until they
settle.

**The single most important open question for the next cycle:** does EU–US adequacy survive
the CJEU appeal? It is the one event that would reshape more of this map than any other, and
everything downstream (European deployments, sovereign-cloud demand, the investment thesis)
turns on it.

## Bottom line

Research: **done.** Position: **strong and internally consistent.** Clear call to action:
**yes — harden for publication (A), assemble the master report (B), then publish on live data
(C).** Nothing else needs researching before this is a finished, defensible work.
